assumptions: critical_swimming_speed_m_s=0.35: about 10 body lengths/s, typical of adult zebrafish; chosen by me.
current_speed_m_s=0.1: well below Ucrit (about 29% of it), so the fish can hold station aerobically; chosen by me.
has_swimbladder=true: zebrafish are physoclistous and have a swimbladder.
bladder_volume_surface_ml=0.02: my estimate, about 2.5% of body volume (0.8 mL), which is a modest value for a freshwater fish.

bladder_volume_at_depth_ml=0.0194: Boyle's law at 0.3 m of fresh water. Pressure goes from 101.325 kPa to about 104.27 kPa (rho*g*h is about 2.94 kPa), so V = 0.02*101.325/104.27 = 0.01943 mL, rounded to 0.0194.
flight_mode='none' and powered=false: declared explicitly. This takes the aerobic-demand laws (C14, E3) out of scope, which is intended for a non-flying design.
Flight fields (airspeed, finArea, CLmax and the rest) are omitted on purpose. They do not apply to a non-flying animal, and inventing values would risk false violations.
notes: I know of no law that blocks the brief. I have not run lean_check, so none of this is verified. Flight-specific and Exocoetidae-scoped laws will return out-of-scope or cannot-evaluate, which is expected. The thermal laws (26 C inside 6.2–41.4 C, Q10 referenced to 28 C), the swimming-speed law (current below Ucrit) and the swimbladder Boyle's-law check should all be evaluated. Energy-budget keys (intake_J_per_day and similar) are left out, because I did not want to invent values that could violate a balance law.
